author: bshastry
content:
Hello! I found a concerning ePBS corner case and would appreciate your opinion. A malicious builder can submit a winning bid with block_hash == parent_block_hash, then withhold its payload. The beacon block is published, but its payload is absent. The next honest proposer correctly builds on the EMPTY parent by reusing that execution hash. However, clients classify the parent as FULL when the child’s parent_block_hash equals the parent bid’s block_hash. Because the malicious builder made those hashes identical, an honest child can never unambiguously encode that the parent was EMPTY.

In testing, Lighthouse and Teku consequently require the nonexistent payload state and stop accepting descendants. Lodestar continues. CC <@755590043632140352> <@586161934425128960>
